chunk_findings.detail: `fingerprint` hashes `load` and `cache` into the key (lines 135-141). These are run-time conditions, not stable machine-class facts. For example, on the same 8-core Linux container with identical `parallel_cap`, `xdist_workers`, Python, ddflow version, and cgroup state, a first sample with `load_ratio=0.20` and a cold cache produces one key; a second sample minutes later with `load_ratio=0.30` and a warm cache produces a different key. The regression detector then cannot compare those samples across commits, contradicting the stated stable-key intent and the docstring’s reason for excluding `git_head`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/env.py:146

chunk_findings.detail: `cgroup_state` claims to read cgroup v1 memory limits but only reads the v1 CPU quota. Given a cgroup v1 memory-limited container where `/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max` and `/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max` are absent, `/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/cpu.cfs_quota_us` is `-1`, and `/sys/fs/cgroup/memory/memory.limit_in_bytes` is `1073741824`, the function never sees the memory limit; it returns `unlimited` (or `unavailable` if the quota file is also absent), even though the environment is limited.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/env.py:69

chunk_findings.detail: `collect` directly uses external environment/filesystem/git probes (`os.cpu_count`, `os.getloadavg`, `platform.system`, `sys.version`, `Path.exists`/`read_text`, and `head_sha`) inside the service instead of going through ports in `ddflow/adapters`. To test `collect` with a fake deterministic environment, callers must monkeypatch module globals such as `os`, `platform`, `sys`, `__version__`, and `head_sha` rather than pass fake adapters, which is the failure mode [r-adapters] is meant to prevent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/env.py:170

chunk_findings.detail: The “leaks nothing” assertion is not a sound leak detector because it searches for raw secrets in a JSON-escaped serialization. On Windows, `str(tmp_path)` contains backslashes; if `collect` leaks the path, `json.dumps` emits it as `C:\\Users\\...` (or the leak may use `as_posix()` with forward slashes), so `str(tmp_path) not in blob` is true even though the path is present. The same false pass happens for non-ASCII identifiers: `getpass.getuser() == "José"` is serialized as `Jos\u00e9`, so a leaked username passes the assertion. This can let identifying data ship while the test reports no leak.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_perf_env.py:test_collect_runs_here_and_leaks_nothing

chunk_findings.detail: cgroup_state documents that it reads cgroup v2 then v1 CPU and memory limits, but it never reads the cgroup v1 memory limit file `/sys/fs/cgroup/memory/memory.limit_in_bytes`. On a cgroup v1 host whose memory controller is mounted and capped (e.g. `/sys/fs/cgroup/memory/memory.limit_in_bytes` contains `1073741824`) while the checked v1 CPU quota file `/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/cpu.cfs_quota_us` is `-1`, this function returns `"unlimited"`; if that CPU file is also absent, it returns `"unavailable"`. Either result misclassifies a memory-limited environment instead of returning `"limited"`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/env.py:cgroup_state

chunk_findings.detail: [r-adapters] This new module directly reaches outside its own process without going through a `ddflow/adapters` port: `_read_file`/`Path.read_text`, `in_container`/`Path.exists`, `cache_state`/`Path.iterdir`, and git via `from ddflow.infra.worktree._merge import head_sha`. A fake git/filesystem backend for tests has no adapter to replace, so the rule’s failure case applies: tests must monkeypatch private modules or stdlib functions instead of swapping one adapter implementation.

chunk_findings.detail: `getpass.getuser()` can raise `KeyError` in POSIX containers where the current UID has no `/etc/passwd` entry and none of `LOGNAME`, `USER`, `LNAME`, or `USERNAME` is set (common with arbitrary UIDs, e.g. OpenShift). In that environment this test errors while building the secret list, before it can test anything about the fingerprint.

chunk_findings.detail: The leak check is not JSON-representation aware: `json.dumps` escapes backslashes as `\\`. On Windows, `str(tmp_path)` and `str(Path.home())` contain single backslashes, so those raw values are not substrings of `blob` even if the fingerprint facts contain the same path in JSON-escaped form. A real path leak on Windows would therefore pass unnoticed.

chunk_findings.detail: `cgroup_state` says it detects “cgroup v2 then v1 cpu and memory limits,” but it only reads v2 `cpu.max`/`memory.max` and v1 `cpu.cfs_quota_us`; it never reads v1 memory limits such as `/sys/fs/cgroup/memory/memory.limit_in_bytes`. On a cgroup v1 machine with a finite memory limit and no readable v2 files, it returns `unavailable` (or `unlimited` if the v1 CPU quota is `-1`), so a memory-limited machine is fingerprinted as unknown/unlimited and gets the wrong key.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/env.py:69

chunk_findings.detail: `cache_state` swallows `OSError` from `d.is_dir()`/`d.iterdir()` and then falls through to `return "cold"`. Given a cache directory that exists but cannot be listed, e.g. one that raises `PermissionError` on `iterdir()`, the function reports `cold` even though the probe did not run. That contradicts the module contract that a failed probe is `unavailable` and causes perf samples to be keyed as cold when the cache state is actually unknown.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/env.py:91

chunk_findings.detail: `Raw` documents that empty means the probe could not run, but `fingerprint` normalizes `cache` to `UNAVAILABLE` while passing `cgroup` through unchanged and using it to derive `vm`. For `Raw(..., container=True, cgroup="")`, the facts contain `cgroup=""` and `vm="no"` instead of `cgroup="unavailable"` and `vm="unknown"`, producing a different key from the same facts with `cgroup=UNAVAILABLE`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/env.py:132

chunk_findings.detail: The new module performs external environment/filesystem/git probing directly in the service: fixed filesystem-layout paths such as `/sys/fs/cgroup/...` and `/.dockerenv`, `os.cpu_count`/`os.getloadavg`, and `head_sha` imported from `ddflow.infra.worktree._merge`. Per [r-adapters], git/filesystem/environment probes should be behind a port in `ddflow/adapters`.

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts that `socket.gethostname()` does not appear anywhere in `blob`, but it also requires `fp.stamp().startswith("env:" + fp.key)`. On a machine whose hostname is the valid value `env` (or a user named `env`), the legitimate stamp prefix contains the “secret” string, so `assert secret not in blob` fails even though no identifying data was leaked.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_perf_env.py:test_collect_runs_here_and_leaks_nothing

chunk_findings.detail: The leak check uses `secret not in json.dumps(...)`, but `json.dumps` escapes non-ASCII and backslashes by default. If a fact leaked a non-ASCII username such as `é`, the JSON blob contains `é`, while `getpass.getuser()` returns the raw `é`, so `é not in blob` is true and the test passes despite the leak. The same escaping issue applies to Windows-style paths containing backslashes.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_perf_env.py:test_collect_runs_here_and_leaks_nothing

chunk_findings.detail: On a cgroup v1 system/container with only a memory limit configured, the v2 paths `/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max` and `/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max` are absent, and `/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/cpu.cfs_quota_us` is `-1`. `cgroup_state` reads only those three files and never reads the cgroup v1 memory limit at `/sys/fs/cgroup/memory/memory.limit_in_bytes`, so `seen` is `[False]` and the function returns `"unlimited"` even though the cgroup is memory-limited. This contradicts the function’s own doc and misclassifies the environment for perf keys.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/env.py:cgroup_state

chunk_findings.detail: If a supplied cache directory exists but cannot be listed, for example `Path('/root')` for a non-root user where `is_dir()` returns True but `iterdir()` raises `PermissionError`, `cache_state` catches the `OSError`, continues, and returns `"cold"` when no other directory has an entry. That violates `collect`’s documented promise that every probe that fails is `"unavailable"`, silently producing false “cold” evidence for an unreadable warm cache.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/env.py:cache_state

chunk_findings.detail: The new module imports `head_sha` directly from `ddflow.infra.worktree._merge` and performs default filesystem probes (`/.dockerenv`, cgroup files) rather than going through a port in `ddflow/adapters`. This violates [r-adapters]: the real git/filesystem dependency is not hidden behind the required single adapter port, so swapping or mocking it still touches this file instead of one adapter implementation.
chunk_findings.title: [r-adapters] ddflow/services/perf/env.py:from ddflow.infra.worktree._merge import head_sha

chunk_findings.detail: The leak check treats any occurrence of the current machine’s actual secret strings as a leak. This is a substring test, so it can fail falsely when the secret coincides with an intentionally non-secret fact or stamp component. For example, `fp.stamp().startswith("env:" + fp.key)` guarantees `blob` contains `"env:"`; on a host whose `socket.gethostname()` is exactly `"env"`, the secret is `"env"` and `assert secret not in blob` fails even though no hostname was leaked. The same false failure occurs if the hostname/user equals another fact value such as `"Linux"` while `fp.facts["os"] == "Linux"`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_perf_env.py:test_collect_runs_here_and_leaks_nothing

chunk_findings.detail: This test calls real external/environment dependencies directly: `socket.gethostname()`, `getpass.getuser()`, `Path.home()`, and the real `E.collect(...)` against the local filesystem, instead of injecting fakes through the adapter port required by [r-adapters]. That violates the rule that external dependencies go through `ddflow/adapters` and tests use fakes, making the test depend on the actual machine identity and filesystem rather than being isolated.
